findings.claim: Item 6 states, from p.16, that Den(<1>^{n+m+k}, L^♭ ⊕ M) = Den(<1>^{n+k}, L^♭) for M self-dual of rank m and L^♭ integral of rank n. This is false. The left side carries the extra factor Den(<1>^{n+m+k}, M) = Π_{i=n+k+1}^{n+m+k}(1 - (-q)^{-i}). The consequence (3.2.1.1), Den(X, L^♭ ⊕ M) = Den(X, L^♭), is nevertheless true, because the normalizing denominator Den(<1>^{n+m+k}, <1>^{n+m}) carries the same factor. No sourceIssue records the misprint. Coordinator note: Verified by the coordinator: with n = m = 1, k = 0 and L^♭ = M = ⟨1⟩ the printed identity reads Den(⟨1⟩², ⟨1⟩²) = Den(⟨1⟩, ⟨1⟩), that is (1 + q^{−1})(1 − q^{−2}) = 1 + q^{−1}.
findings.evidence:
p.16, §3.2: 'for any self-dual lattice M of rank(M) = m and any integral lattice L^♭ of rank(L^♭) = n, we have Den(<1>^{n+m+k}, L^♭ ⊕ M) = Den(<1>^{n+k}, L^♭) and therefore we obtain a cancellation law: Den(X, L^♭ ⊕ M) = Den(X, L^♭). (3.2.1.1)'.
